title: Letter 2 — On the Certain Truth of God's Word
attribution_note: Letter 2 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance. This letter and the three following it (Letters 3–5) were originally written by St Tikhon as one continuous treatise, On Faith, which he later divided into four letters for this collection; each is translated here as its own complete letter.

sections.heading: Every promise of God has already come true once

pairs.en: You ask me to write you something for the strengthening of our Christian faith. — Very well. This is needed always, but especially in these days, when so many devices of men are rising up.

I set before you first of all that everything God reveals or speaks, promises or foretells, in Holy Scripture, is unchangeably true and sure, and cannot be otherwise. And the certainty of this truth is explained and shown from His events, prophecies and promises, already fulfilled in the very deed. Attend to what follows, and you will learn on what the holy faith is founded.

God foretold to our first parents in paradise that they would *“die the death”* if they ate of the forbidden tree — and so it was: they ate, and died. [Genesis 2:17; 3:19] God told Noah what would come upon the earth — and the flood came. [Genesis 6:17; 7:17–21] God promised Abraham to give him a son [Genesis 15:4–5] — and gave him one in his old age. [Genesis 21:2–3] God told Abraham that his descendants would be strangers in a foreign land, and would be afflicted, and humbled there, and would come out from there with great possessions [Genesis 15:13–14] — and so it was. They went down into Egypt, and were afflicted and oppressed there by the Egyptians, and came out from there with great possessions, as we read in the books of Moses and in Psalm 104. God promised Abraham to give him and his seed the land of Canaan for an inheritance — and gave it. [Read of this the books of Moses and of Joshua, and Psalms 87 and 104, and the rest.] He promised to send Christ the Saviour into the world — and so it was: He sent Him, and those who *“have loved His appearing”* are saved. [2 Timothy 4:8] And whatever, of what was foretold of Him in the Old Testament, was due to be fulfilled before this present age, has all been fulfilled exactly as it was foretold.

sections.heading: What was foretold of Christ's coming and His life

pairs.en: Attend, then, and consider the prophecies and their fulfilments, and let your faith be strengthened. It was foretold that Christ would be born of a Virgin who had known no marriage: *“Behold, a virgin shall conceive in the womb, and bear a Son, and they shall call His name Emmanuel.”* [Isaiah 7:14] And so it was: Christ was born of a Virgin. [Matthew 1:18]

It was foretold that He would be born of the tribe of Judah, in the city of Bethlehem: *“And thou, Bethlehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall come forth unto Me He that is to be ruler in Israel.”* [Micah 5:2] — this very prophecy the chief priests and the scribes of the people brought before King Herod. [Matthew 2:5–6] And so it was: *“For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of the tribe of Judah;* *Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea.”* [Hebrews 7:14; Matthew 2:1; Luke 2:7, 11]

It was foretold that He would be born of the seed of David [2 Samuel 7:12; Isaiah 11:1; Psalm 131:11], and so the Jews themselves believed and said: *“Hath not the Scripture said, that Christ cometh of the seed of David, and out of the town of Bethlehem, where David was?”* [John 7:42] And so it was: Christ *“was made of the seed of David according to the flesh.”* [Romans 1:3; Luke 1:66; Matthew 1, and elsewhere] For this Christ is also called *“the Son of David.”* [Matthew 20:30; 9:27; 22, and elsewhere]

It was foretold that men would come with gifts to worship the new-born Christ: *“The kings of Tarshish and of the isles shall bring presents; the kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts.”* [Psalm 71:10] And so it was: three wise kings came from the east to worship the infant Christ, and *“fell down, and worshipped Him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto Him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.”* [Matthew 2:11]

Nor did Holy Scripture keep silence about this: that at Christ's birth children would be slain in the place of His birth, and the voice of their mothers be heard in the country round about: *“A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, and bitter weeping;* *Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted for her children, because they are not.”* [Jeremiah 31:15] And the Scripture was fulfilled: all the children from two years old and under were killed in Bethlehem, where Christ was born, and in all its borders, as the holy evangelist records. [Matthew 2:16–18]

The flight into Egypt, and Christ's return out of Egypt, was foretold beforehand: *“Out of Egypt have I called My son,”* said the Lord [Hosea 11:1] — and this same prophecy the evangelist applies to Christ. And so it was: Christ our Lord fled as an Infant into Egypt from Herod the murderer, and after his death was brought back from there. [Matthew 2:14–15, 21]

The Lord promised to send His Angel before the face of His Christ: *“Behold, I send My messenger before Thy face, which shall prepare Thy way before Thee,”* said God to Christ His Son. [Malachi 3:1; Matthew 11:10] And so it was: an angel was sent before Jesus Christ — not a bodiless angel, but one clothed in flesh, the great John, of whom Christ Himself bore witness, saying: *“This is he, of whom it is written, Behold, I send...”* and the rest. [Matthew 11:10; Luke 7:27] This angel of God went before Christ and prepared His way, saying: *“There cometh One mightier than I after me, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to stoop down and unloose.”* [Mark 1:2, 7; Matthew 3:1; Luke 3:16; John 1:27] And he pointed out to the people the Christ who had come and appeared, saying: *“Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.* *This is He of whom I said, After me cometh a Man which is preferred before me: for He was before me.”* [John 1:29–30] *“There was a man sent from God, whose name was John.* *The same came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light”* — that is, of Christ — *“that all men through him might believe.”* [John 1:6–7] For this reason holy John is called by the Church the Forerunner of Christ, as one who appeared before Christ's coming.

It was foretold that Christ would begin His holy preaching in Galilee: *“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles; the people which sat in darkness saw great light; and to them which sat in the region and shadow of death light is sprung up.”* [Isaiah 9:1–2; Matthew 4:15–16] So it was: there first the Light of the world, Christ, appeared; there this Light shone upon them that sat in darkness and enlightened them; there Jesus, our Light, *“began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.”* [Matthew 4:14–17; Mark 1:14–15]

It was foretold that Christ would teach in parables: *“I will open my mouth in a parable: I will utter dark sayings of old,”* Christ spoke through the prophet. [Psalm 77:2] So it was: Jesus Christ taught in parables. [Matthew 13:34–35] Read His Gospel.

It was foretold that many would not listen to His holy teaching, and would not believe Him, and would not receive Him. *“Go,”* said the Lord, *“and tell this people”* (the Jews): *“Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not.* *For the heart of this people is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.”* [Isaiah 6:9–10] And so it was: the scribes, the Pharisees and very many other Jews did not listen to Christ's teaching, and did not believe Him, and did not receive Him. *“He came unto His own, and His own received Him not.”* [John 1:11] Read the Gospel, and see how the Jews who had waited for Him set themselves against Christ.

It was foretold that Christ would bring a good and joyful message to men: *“The Spirit of the Lord God is upon Me; because the Lord hath anointed Me to preach good tidings unto the meek;* *He hath sent Me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound, to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord,”* the prophet said in the person of Christ. [Isaiah 61:1–3] So it was: Christ Himself applied this very prophecy to Himself before the Jews: *“And He began to say unto them, This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.”* [Luke 4:17–21] He, *“when He came, preached peace to us.”* [Ephesians 2:17] He preached: *“For God so loved the world, that He gave His only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in Him should not perish, but have everlasting life.* *For God sent not His Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through Him might be saved.”* [John 3:16–17] What can be more joyful to perishing sinners than this word: *“The Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost”*? [Luke 19:10]

It was foretold that Christ would work many wonders: *“Then”* — at Christ's coming — *“the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.* *Then shall the lame man leap as an hart, and the tongue of the dumb sing.”* [Isaiah 35:5–6; 29:18] And it was fulfilled exactly so: how many wonders and signs Christ worked, the Gospel bears witness. By His word and power the blind received sight, the deaf hearing, the dumb speech, the lame their walking, the lepers cleansing, the paralysed their healing, and the dead were raised up. And when John's disciples asked Christ, in their teacher's name: *“Art thou He that should come, or look we for another?”* — He Himself pointed to this very prophecy of Isaiah: *“Go your way, and tell John what things ye have seen and heard: how that the blind see, and the lame walk,”* and the rest — showing that it was even then fulfilled. [Matthew 11:3–5; Luke 7:19, 22]

sections.heading: What was foretold of Christ's suffering and death

pairs.en: It was foretold that many of the Jews would hate Christ, Him who had been promised and sent to them and whom they had awaited: *“Those that hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of mine head,”* says the Psalmist in the person of Christ [Psalm 68:5]; and again: *“They rewarded Me evil for good, and hatred for My love.”* [Psalm 108:5] And so it was: the scribes, the Pharisees and the rest of the Jews hated Christ, and for this reproached, reviled, blasphemed and persecuted Him. Read the Gospel and you will see it. Of this the Lord Himself speaks, quoting the very prophecy of their hatred: *“But now have they both seen and hated both Me and My Father.* *But this cometh to pass, that the word might be fulfilled that is written in their law, They hated Me without a cause.”* [John 15:24–25]

It was foretold how gentle, meek, approachable and humble Christ would be: *“Behold My Servant, whom I have chosen;* *My Beloved, in whom My soul is well pleased: I will put My Spirit upon Him, and He shall show judgment to the Gentiles.* *He shall not strive, nor cry; neither shall any man hear His voice in the streets.* *A bruised reed shall He not break, and smoking flax shall He not quench, till He send forth judgment unto victory.”* [Isaiah 42:1–3; Matthew 12:18–20] So it was. Read the Gospel, and it will show you His most holy and divine ways, which He also teaches us to imitate: *“Learn of Me; for I am meek and lowly in heart.”* [Matthew 11:29]

It was foretold that Christ would enter the city of Jerusalem, where He was to suffer, riding upon a young ass: *“Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee, just and having salvation, meek, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.”* [Zechariah 9:9] He would enter amid the shouting of a great multitude: *“Blessed is He that cometh in the name of the Lord!”* [Psalm 117:26] And so it was: so Christ entered Jerusalem, going to His voluntary passion. *“And the multitudes that went before, and that followed, cried, saying, Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is He that cometh in the name of the Lord;* *Hosanna in the highest.”* [Matthew 21:9; Mark 11:1–10; Luke 19:29–38; John 12:12–15]

It was foretold that one of Christ's own closest disciples would betray Him: *“Mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of My bread, hath lifted up his heel against Me,”* Christ spoke through the prophet [Psalm 40:10; John 13:18], of which mention is also made in Psalm 108. And so it was: Judas, one of the twelve, betrayed Christ: *“Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief priests, and said, What will ye give me, and I will deliver Him unto you?”* [Matthew 26:14–15; Acts 1:16]

Nor did Scripture keep silence about this: that He would be sold for thirty pieces of silver: *“So they weighed for My price thirty pieces of silver.”* [Zechariah 11:12] And so it was: the Priceless One was sold by the traitor for thirty pieces of silver. [Matthew 26:15; 27:3, 5, 9–10]

It was written of Christ: *“I will smite the Shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered.”* [Zechariah 13:7; Matthew 26:31] And so it was: Christ, our Shepherd, was struck, and His sheep, the apostles, scattered: *“Then all the disciples forsook Him”* — Christ — *“and fled.”* [Matthew 26:56]

The kingly prophet sang, foreseeing the lawless council of lawless men against Christ: *“Why do the heathen rage, and the people imagine a vain thing?* *The kings of the earth stood up, and the rulers were gathered together against the Lord, and against His Christ.”* [Psalm 2:1–2; Acts 4:25–26] And so it was: *“Then assembled the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders of the people, unto the palace of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas, and consulted that they might take Jesus by subtlety, and kill Him.”* [Matthew 26:3–4] *“For of a truth against Thy holy Child Jesus, whom Thou hast anointed, both Herod, and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles, and the people of Israel, were gathered together, for to do whatsoever Thy hand and Thy counsel determined before to be done,”* so the apostles prayed to the Lord. [Acts 4:25–28] The rulers of the people, and Pilate the Gentile, judged Christ and condemned Him to death. *“Herod with his men of war, having set Him at nought, and mocked Him, arrayed Him in a gorgeous robe, and sent Him again to Pilate.”* [Luke 23:11] The Jews cried out against Christ to Pilate: *“Away with Him, away with Him, crucify Him!”* [John 19:15] Pilate's soldiers, *“they stripped Him, and put on Him a scarlet robe.* *And when they had platted a crown of thorns, they put it upon His head, and a reed in His right hand: and they bowed the knee before Him, and mocked Him, saying, Hail, King of the Jews! and they spit upon Him, and took the reed, and smote Him on the head,”* and the rest. [Matthew 27:28–30] Read the Gospel history of Christ's passion, and see how *“all were gathered together against Christ the Lord.”*

It was foretold beforehand that there would be false witnesses against Christ: *“False witnesses did rise up against Me, they asked Me of things that I knew not.”* [Psalm 34:11] And so it was: what false witnesses were not raised up against Christ, and what false testimonies did the chief priests and elders, and the whole council, not seek against Him! Read the Gospel of the passion and see.

It was written of Christ: *“I gave My back to the smiters, and My cheeks to them that plucked off the hair: I hid not My face from shame and spitting.”* [Isaiah 50:6] And so it was: Jesus Christ our Lord was scourged, wounded, struck on the face and spat upon. Read the Gospel, and it will set this before you.

It was written of Christ: *“He hath no form nor comeliness; and we have seen Him, and there is no beauty that we should desire Him.* *He is despised and rejected of men.”* [Isaiah 53:2–3] So it was. [Philippians 2:7–8] Every brutal inhumanity and malice was worked upon Him by His enemies. No evildoer or robber was ever so brought low, so dishonoured, so ill-used, so mocked, so wounded and so torn as Christ; and He was set before the Jews by Pilate as a fearful spectacle: *“Behold the Man!”* [John 19:5] Behold the Man — and no longer having the form of a man!

It was foretold beforehand of Christ: *“He is brought as a sheep to the slaughter, and as a lamb before its shearer is dumb, so He opened not His mouth.”* [Isaiah 53:7] And so it was fulfilled. Jesus Christ opened not His mouth before His enemies. He opened it not in the house of Caiaphas, before the lawless council: *“But Jesus held His peace.”* [Matthew 26:63; Mark 14:61] He opened it not before the governor: *“He answered him to never a word; insomuch that the governor marvelled greatly.”* [Matthew 27:14] He opened it not before Herod: *“He answered him nothing.”* [Luke 23:9] Nor did He answer before His other enemies, who blasphemed, reviled, reproached and slandered Him, and mocked and wounded Him — as dumb as a lamb before its shearers. He was led to crucifixion and death, as a sheep to the slaughter.
It was written of Christ: *“They pierced My hands and My feet.”* [Psalm 21:17] And so it was: they pierced His hands and His feet when they nailed Him to the cross. Read the Gospel and see.

It was written: *“Thy life shall hang in doubt before thee.”* [Deuteronomy 28:66] And it was fulfilled thus: Life itself, Jesus Christ, was hanged upon the tree of the cross, and the eyes of all beheld Him. *“And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness”* [Numbers 21:9], *“even so was the Son of man lifted up, that whosoever believeth in Him should not perish, but have eternal life.”* [John 3:14–15; 19:18]

It was written: *“And He was numbered with the transgressors.”* [Isaiah 53:12] And this was fulfilled in Jesus Christ: He was crucified and hanged between two robbers, and so He who alone is righteous and holy was *“numbered with the transgressors.”* [Mark 15:27–28; Luke 22:37; 23:33]

It was written: *“And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the Lord God, that I will cause the sun to go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the clear day.”* [Amos 8:9] And so it was: the sun was darkened at the crucifixion of our Lord Jesus Christ. *“Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land unto the ninth hour.”* [Matthew 27:45]

It was written of Christ: *“They gave Me also gall to eat; and in My thirst they gave Me vinegar to drink.”* [Psalm 68:22] And so it was fulfilled: they gave Jesus vinegar mixed with gall. *“They gave Him vinegar to drink mingled with gall.”* [Matthew 27:34, 48]

It was written of Christ: *“All they that see Me laugh Me to scorn: they shoot out the lip, they shake the head, saying, He trusted in the Lord that He would deliver Him: let Him deliver Him, seeing He delighted in Him.”* [Psalm 21:8–9] And this was fulfilled in Christ suffering. *“And they that passed by reviled Him, wagging their heads, and saying, Thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days, save Thyself.* *If Thou be the Son of God, come down from the cross.* *Likewise also the chief priests mocking Him, with the scribes and elders, said, He saved others;* *Himself He cannot save.* *If He be the King of Israel, let Him now come down from the cross, and we will believe Him.* *He trusted in God; let Him deliver Him now, if He will have Him,”* and the rest. [Matthew 27:39–43]

It was written: *“They part My garments among them, and cast lots upon My vesture,”* Christ spoke through the Psalmist. [Psalm 21:19] And so it was: *“they that crucified Him parted His garments, casting lots upon them, what every man should take.”* [Mark 15:24; Matthew 27:35; Luke 23:34; John 19:24]

It was written of Christ's death: *“Into Thy hands I commit My spirit.”* [Psalm 30:6] And so it was: these very words Christ spoke as He died on the cross: *“Father, into Thy hands I commend My spirit: and having said thus, He gave up the ghost.”* [Luke 23:46]

It was written of Christ: *“Surely He hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem Him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted.* *But He was wounded for our transgressions, He was bruised for our iniquities,”* and the rest. [Isaiah 53:4–5] So it was: Christ suffered for our sins. *“Who was delivered for our offences”* [Romans 4:25; 1 Corinthians 15:3]; *“who His own self bare our sins in His own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness.”* [1 Peter 2:24]

The sacrifices that were burned outside the camp prefigured that Christ must suffer and die for us outside the city. So *“Jesus also, that He might sanctify the people with His own blood, suffered outside the gate.”* [Hebrews 13:12]

So Jesus Christ came into the world and fulfilled everything that was written of Him. And *“He died for our sins according to the scriptures; and He was buried, and He rose again the third day according to the scriptures”* [1 Corinthians 15:3–4], and *“He was received up into heaven, and sat on the right hand of God.”* [Mark 16:19]

sections.heading: The Church, the nations, and the two Testaments

pairs.en: Nor did Scripture keep silence about this: that Christ would gather disciples to Himself and send them into all the world. *“Instead of thy fathers shall be thy children, whom thou shalt make princes in all the earth.”* [Psalm 44:17] And so it was: Christ gathered twelve apostles, and, as King of heaven and earth, made them princes over all the earth, that upon Him, as upon the rock, they might build His Church. They preached Him throughout the whole world. *“Their sound went into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.”* [Psalm 18:5; Romans 10:18]

It is also declared in Holy Scripture that the pagan nations would turn to the true God. *“All the ends of the world shall remember and turn unto the Lord: and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before Him.”* [Psalm 21:28] *“I will call them My people, which were not My people; and her beloved, which was not beloved.* *And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not My people; there shall they be called the children of the living God.”* [Hosea 2:23; 1:10; Romans 9:25–26] *“I was found of them that sought Me not;* *I was made manifest unto them that asked not after Me.”* [Isaiah 65:1; Romans 10:20] This was fulfilled at Christ's coming. All the ends of the earth have remembered and turned to the Lord, and all the nations and tribes worship before Him. They honour and glorify the true and living God, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, having cast down and spat upon their vain idols. *“From the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same, the name of the Lord is praised.”* [Psalm 112:3; Malachi 1:11]

And so you see that the Scripture of the Old Testament proclaimed that Christ was 'to come,' and the Scripture of the New Testament proclaims that He has already 'come.' And as Scripture foretold of Christ, so it has all been fulfilled, and what was fulfilled is proclaimed in the New Testament. And as the faithful of the Old Testament believed in Him who was 'to come,' so we now believe in Christ who has already come.

But just as the prophecies of the Old Testament, which were due to be fulfilled before this day, have been fulfilled, so too has what was foretold in the New Testament, and what was due to be fulfilled by now, been fulfilled. Christ foretold that one of His disciples would betray Him, that all His disciples would forsake Him, that Peter the apostle would deny Him three times, that He must suffer much from the elders and scribes, and so on — and so it was. He foretold that the city of Jerusalem and the temple in it would be laid waste, and not one stone left upon another. And so it was: the city and the temple were destroyed by the Romans, as we read in history. He foretold that His faithful would endure persecution. So it was: godly souls have been hated, persecuted and ill-treated by all, and to the end of the age *“all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.”* [2 Timothy 3:12]

He said that *“the gates of hell shall not prevail against”* His Church. [Matthew 16:18] And so it is: however hard Satan has striven, through the Jews, through kings, through the wise men of this age, through heretics and his other servants, to overcome and destroy the Church of Christ, he has achieved nothing. It stands, and will stand firm, founded upon the Rock. And the Rock is Christ, the Son of the living God, of whom it is written: *“Behold, I lay in Zion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on Him shall not be confounded.”* [Isaiah 28:16; Psalm 117:22; Matthew 21:42; Acts 4:11; 1 Peter 2:7; Romans 9:33; 1 Corinthians 3:11; Ephesians 2:20] Christ promised to send the Holy Spirit to the apostles and to all the faithful. [Joel 2:28, 32; John 7:38–39] And this was fulfilled: the Holy Spirit came upon the apostles and upon all flesh that believed. [Acts 2:1–21] Read the Gospel of this and see.

You see, then, that everything Holy Scripture says is true, without falsehood, and *“worthy of all acceptation.”* What it says, then, is exact and cannot be revoked. From this we rightly and firmly conclude:

1) All the prophecies and promises of God that were due to be fulfilled by this day have been fulfilled; so too will those be fulfilled that we still wait for and hope for. We hope, according to Scripture, for the resurrection of the dead — it will most certainly be. *“The dead shall live, and shall rise out of their graves.”* [Isaiah 26:19; see also Ezekiel 37:1–13; Daniel 12:2; John 5:25, 28; 11:25–26; 1 Corinthians 15:12–56] We wait for Christ's second coming and His dread judgment — it will most certainly come to pass. Christ will come to judge the living and the dead, and all will receive according to their works. [Acts 17:31; 1:11; Psalm 6:9; 2 Corinthians 5:10] God has promised His faithful to give them eternal life, and we hope, according to His promise, to partake of eternal life — this will most certainly be: *“the righteous”* shall *“live for evermore”* [Wisdom 5:15], and shall *“inherit the kingdom prepared for”* them *“from the foundation of the world”* [Matthew 25:34]; *“the righteous shall shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father.”* [Matthew 13:43] It is declared in Scripture that there will be eternal torment for the unrepentant sinner — and this too will be. For them there will be eternal fire, outer darkness, gnashing of teeth, the worm that never sleeps, and all the rest. Everything that has been promised and foretold by God will come to pass. It must all be fulfilled, for God's word and promise is true, sure and without falsehood, as was said above. *“Heaven and earth shall pass away, but My words shall not pass away.”* [Matthew 24:35; Mark 13:31; Luke 21:33] And this is as true and certain as it is true that yesterday was, and today is.

2) What Holy Scripture declares to us about God and God's attributes, and about all else, is exactly so, and must be believed without doubt. It teaches us that God is one in nature, yet threefold in Persons — Father, Son and Holy Spirit; a God without beginning, without end, everlasting, immortal, everywhere present, all-knowing, all-good, merciful, righteous, true, immaterial spirit, all-wise, incomprehensible, and the rest. So it exactly is. So the Holy Church believes and confesses, and so it venerates the Godhead in three Persons.

3) Holy Scripture teaches that God, three in Person, created the world, heaven and earth and all that fills them, out of nothing, by His will and word. *“Whatsoever He pleased, that He hath done.* *He spake, and it was done;* *He commanded, and it stood fast.”* [Psalm 113:11; 32:9] So it is. There is no doubt at all about this, nor should there be among Orthodox Christians. So the whole Holy Church believes and confesses — though the creation of the world is also known by natural reason, since nothing comes to be of itself, but receives its beginning of being from another: no craft exists without a craftsman, and so on.

4) Holy Scripture declares to us that God, three in Person, cares for the world He has created, and especially for the human race, and above all for His own Church. So it exactly is. We acknowledge and see His wise and wondrous Providence over all and every creature, so that *“not one of the little sparrows falls to the ground without the will”* of the heavenly Father. [Matthew 10:29] But Holy Scripture itself is a sign of God's wondrous Providence for us. For what greater gift could there be from God to us than Holy Scripture? It *“shineth”* for us *“as a light”* to those sitting in a *“dark place,”* walking amid the snares of the enemy, and journeying as strangers in this world's foreign land. Natural reason itself proves God's Providence over the world. For if God is the Creator of the world, He is also its Provider. What householder does not care for his own house, what king for his own realm? God is Master of the whole world; all things belong to Him — heaven and earth and all that fills them are His; He is Lord and King of heaven and earth, as of His own creation. And how could it be that He should abandon His creation without care? It cannot be so. So the whole Holy Church confesses.

5) Scripture proclaims that Christ, foreordained before the ages, promised by God, proclaimed by the prophets, awaited by the world, came into the world to save sinners, and was born of the most holy and undefiled Virgin for our salvation, and lived on earth, suffered, died and rose from the dead, and, having thus accomplished our salvation, ascended into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God the Father. So it is.

6) Scripture proclaims that Christ our Lord is true God and true man, not divided into two persons, but known unconfusedly in two natures. So it is. So the Holy Church confesses Him, honours Him, and worships Him.

7) Scripture proclaims that there is no other way to obtain eternal salvation than by true and living faith in our Lord Jesus Christ — a faith that shows itself by confession and by love. *“Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.”* [Acts 4:11–12] *“He is made unto us wisdom from God, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption.”* [1 Corinthians 1:30] For this He is named, confessed and believed by His Church to be the one Redeemer, Deliverer and Saviour of the world. And all who are saved at all, are saved in His name alone. So it is, exactly and without doubt.

8) Scripture teaches that *“wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and narrow is the gate, and strait is the way, which leadeth unto life.”* [Matthew 7:13–14, and elsewhere] So it is. Whoever wants to be saved must deny himself and, taking up his cross, follow Christ. [Matthew 16:24]

9) Scripture declares that there are good angels and evil angels. So it is. Some tempt, seduce, deceive, war against us, lead us to evil, and try to bring us with them into eternal ruin; but others camp about us and keep us, guide us to what is good, rejoice over our repentance, and carry the holy souls that depart from here into the bosom of Abraham.

10) Scripture declares that true Christians *“have fellowship with the Father, and with His Son Jesus Christ”* [1 John 1:3]; that they are *“the sons of God”* [1 John 3:1; Romans 8:17; John 1:12; Galatians 3:26], *“members”* of Christ [1 Corinthians 6:15; Ephesians 5:30], the *“temple of the Holy Ghost”* [1 Corinthians 3:16; 6:19; Romans 8:9]. And so it is in very truth: they have this great mercy from God, and this unspeakable honour.

11) Scripture declares that in the most holy Eucharist there is the true Body of Christ and the true Blood of Christ, of which Christians partake. And this is truly so. So the whole Holy Church believes and confesses.

So too everything else that Holy Scripture declares and says is exactly so. For Holy Scripture is the true Word of God, which can neither deceive nor lie, any more than God Himself can. It ought to be believed more than our own senses, and more than the whole world. Our senses, and the whole world, can more easily deceive us than Holy Scripture can. Found your faith, then, on this firm and unshaken foundation. And if some satanic temptation of the mind, or some evil and corrupted man, should set the contrary before you, drive that cunning and crafty serpent from you with the sword of the Word of God and the faith of the Holy Orthodox Church, saying within yourself, and confessing with your lips: “So the holy Word of God teaches us, and so the Holy Church believes and confesses. I believe and confess as the Word of God reveals and teaches, and as the Church believes and confesses.”
Be saved.
